thread_summary: Four lines, one story (docs/STORY.md section 0): a complex number is a move (turn, then stretch; the Cartesian address says where it sits, the polar address says the move that makes it; add in Cartesian, multiply in polar); a turn has many names (arg z is the staircase, Arg z the home step, z the dot on the floor; every angle problem is settled by which names it needs: any, all, home or continuous); a function moves every point at once (strokes carried on one clock; parametrize, push forward, eliminate t); and differentiable means one move up close (the direction circle A + B e^{-2i phi} shrinks to a point, Cauchy-Riemann says no mirror, and f'(z0) is a complex number with the same two addresses as line 1). Iteration 2 makes the story something the student DOES rather than reads: two decision chips (Address, Names) on every problem; the move glyph beside every complex number including f'; a Rehearsal Room with fresh numbers for all 29 problem types that opens the station with those numbers; one guided Walk through 22 stops with a persistent bar and auto-ticks; the Lab as a diary (planes first, live ink, replay, pages, the opening example framed off the axis); five manim videos with narration carrying the spine; three pictures made to say what they mean (the staircase ribbon, the arithmetic log ruler, the 4D shadows side by side); the index as a deck; and a chart-like identity.

12 goals: 3 in wave 0 (the shared modules every consumer imports: i2-decisions-kit, i2-generators, i2-media-core), 9 in wave 1 (the Walk and identity in the shell, the Rehearsal Room, the Lab diary, the three pictures, the home map and index deck, the chips/glyph/values pass over the fifteen remaining stations, and three video goals carrying the five scenes).
